subject: DPA clarifications - data handling (Acme Payments)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA clarifications - data handling (Acme Payments)

Hi Alicia,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap and the outstanding items we promised to follow up on from the discovery:

- Roles: Confirmation that Acme Payments will be the Data Controller and Redwood Inference the Data Processor for the transactional/telemetry data generated by your integration.
- PII scope: You mentioned account IDs, email addresses, and payment identifiers - please confirm the exact fields you consider PII for the integration.
- Retention: Your req for 90 days default logs + option for 30/365 day configs.
- Logging/audit: Need for immutable audit logs and per-request tracing for investigations.
- Data residency: EU region requirement for European customers; primary tenancy in us-east for US workloads.
- Subprocessors: Requesting our subprocessors list and any planned additions.
- Breach notice: You flagged a requirement for a 72-hour notification window and additional remediation support.

I've attached a short DPA summary that highlights our standard positions and the subprocessors list (redacted); Connor will follow up with the full subprocessors CSV and our SOC 2 Type II report under NDA.

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm the PII fields and whether the 72-hour breach notification is an absolute requirement?
2) Connor and Rishi can join a quick 30-minute call with your security/legal team if you'd prefer to run through the DPA line-by-line.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Summary.pdf (summary), acme_questionnaire.xlsx (your intake)

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acmepayments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acmepayments.com
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications - data handling (Acme Payments)

Hi Marissa,

Appreciate the recap. A few clarifying Qs from our security team:

- Please confirm Redwood's legal role in writing: will Redwood sign as Processor and will Acme remain Controller? We cannot accept language that makes us a Processor/Controller joint custodian.
- Subprocessors: please provide a current list (name, country, purpose) and confirm you'll notify us 30 days prior to any new subprocessor onboarding.
- Breach notice: our legal is asking for a guaranteed 72-hour notification for incidents that materially impact Acme data. Is that standard in your DPA?
- Data residency options: we need to ensure EU customer data at rest and in transit remains in the EU; can you confirm region-based tenancy and that backups are region-bound?
- Audit evidence: we'll need SOC 2 Type II and encryption-at-rest details. Can SOC2 be provided under an NDA and is your KMS cloud-managed or customer-managed?

Attached: Acme_Security_Questions.xlsx

Can we do a call tomorrow morning (Thu) at 9:30am PT to walk through?

Thanks,
Alicia Gomez
Security Analyst
Acme Payments
agomez@acmepayments.com

Subject: Re: DPA clarifications - data handling (Acme Payments)

Hi Alicia,

Thanks - answers inline below and attaching the files you requested.

- Roles: Redwood will sign the DPA as Processor. Customers remain Controller. We will not assert joint-controller responsibilities in the standard DPA.
- Subprocessors: attached subprocessors_list_20260701.csv (columns: name, country, purpose). We agree to notify customers of new subprocessors; our standard notice period is 30 days for material subprocessors. If you need contractual prior-approval, we can scope that in as an exception.
- Breach notice: Redwood's standard DPA includes a 72-hour notification SLA for incidents that materially affect customer data. We will escalate to your security contact and include remediation steps and timelines.
- Data residency: We support tenancy in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. For EU-only customers we can restrict data at rest and backups to eu-west-1. All data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (AES-256). KMS: we use cloud KMS with customer-managed keys available for private deployments; for hosted customers we offer a KMS bring-your-own-key option via customer-managed keys in supported clouds.
- Audit evidence: SOC 2 Type II redacted report attached (SOC2_redacted.pdf). We can provide the full report under NDA.

Attachments: subprocessors_list_20260701.csv, SOC2_redacted.pdf, Redwood_DPA_Summary.pdf

Proposed next step: agree time for a 30-min review with your security/legal team; Marissa - can you confirm Thu 9:30am PT works?

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien
Head of Solutions
Redwood Inference
